question:
A **concave mirror** is used in an optics experiment using Cartesian sign convention. With an object placed at $u=-48\,\text{cm}$, a real image is obtained on a screen at $v=-24\,\text{cm}$.

A student now claims:
“Since the image is real and diminished, if I move the object $24\,\text{cm}$ closer to the mirror, to $u=-24\,\text{cm}$, the image will still be real and will form exactly at the centre of curvature.”

For the same mirror, when the object is at $u=-24\,\text{cm}$, determine the new image distance $v$ and evaluate the claim.

options.A: Claim is false; $v=-48\,\text{cm}$ (real image at $48\,\text{cm}$ in front of the mirror).
options.B: Claim is true; $v=-32\,\text{cm}$ (real image at the centre of curvature).
options.C: Claim is false; $v=+48\,\text{cm}$ (virtual image behind the mirror).
options.D: Claim is true; $v=-16\,\text{cm}$ (real image at focus).
